Your work days are brighter here. 
 We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.
 About the Team 
You'll join the AI Products team, where we build Workday's AI agents from the ground up. Our mission is to bring these agents to life inside real customer environments — testing them against real data, real workflows, and real use cases.
We're early in the agent lifecycle, which means the work here is hands-on, fast-moving, and genuinely entrepreneurial: you'll often help write the playbook for how Workday deploys a new agent, rather than follow one that already exists. If you want to be close to the product at the exact moment it's taking shape, and to see your fieldwork directly change the product, this is the team to build inside. 
 About the Role 
 As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work directly with some of Workday's most important early customers to deploy, configure, and improve our AI products and agents. You'll work alongside our product and engineering teams as an extension of our internal product managers, playing a central role in agent Early Access (EA) programs and running the customer deployments inside them. 
 Your mission is to make the product better by putting it to work in a live customer environment. A successful deployment is both a win for the customer and proof that the product is improving, so making early customers successful matters just as much as hardening the agent itself. You'll often be the first person at Workday to run a deployment of a given agent, so good judgment, clear communication, ownership, and organization will matter as much as technical curiosity. 
 Every deployment will surface something the product wasn't built for yet, so creative problem-solving and a "yes, and" mindset are core to this role: instead of telling a customer that something isn't possible, you'll find a way to solve their use case with what exists today, bring them along on what's coming next, and turn the gap into clear feedback for product and engineering. 
 In this role, you will: 
 Lead customer discovery to understand each customer's goals and what success looks like for them 
 Act as the day-to-day lead for design partners and EA customers: setting and resetting expectations, working with senior leaders across HR, Finance, and IT, and repairing relationships when a deployment hits a rough patch 
 Run EA deployments end to end: implement, configure, debug, and improve the solution through rapid iteration with direct customer feedback 
 Interpret customer tenant data, configuration, and unique workflows, and how the agent performs against them 
 Triage every issue quickly, sorting bugs from configuration issues, product gaps, and change-management needs, prioritize them, and route each to the right owner with the right urgency 
 Keep customers and internal teams updated on status, risks, and next steps 
 Turn customer feedback into clear problem statements, reproduction details, and evidence that product and engineering can act on to make the agent more accurate and reliable 
 Help define, measure, and assess the pre-GA stage gates and graduation scorecard for your product 
 Build playbooks, configuration patterns, and known-issue guides, and hand them off to the teams that scale deployments and build documentation 
 Partner closely with your product's program manager and the Workday Services lead on each customer project 
 Stay engaged through early GA until your product meets its graduation criteria, and remain a point of contact for major customers and future releases afterward 
 About You

 7+ years of experience in product management, consulting, solutions engineering, implementation, or customer support within complex enterprise environments 
 Willingness and ability to travel up to 20% to customer sites as needed

 10+ years of experience in technical product management, solution architecture, forward deployed engineering, enterprise implementation, or principal-level consulting within complex enterprise SaaS ecosystems 
 Experience driving complex AI/ML, automation, or enterprise software deployments at scale with Fortune 500 executive stakeholders 
 Willingness and ability to travel up to 20% to customer sites as needed 
 Other Qualifications 
 A demonstrated history of entrepreneurial ownership: you've built something from scratch, worked without a playbook, or driven an initiative end to end in an ambiguous environment, and you're energized by figuring out the right path when one doesn't already exist 
 Experience managing strategic customer relationships with senior leaders in key accounts — setting and resetting expectations, navigating organizational change, and rebuilding trust when a project hits a rough patch 
 Working knowledge of Workday, including business processes, security and permissions, tenant configuration, integrations, and how customers implement and govern Workday, so you can read a customer's tenant and understand how the agent will behave inside it

 Posting Statement 
 Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education. 
At Salesforce, we believe in equitable compensation practices that reflect the dynamic nature of labor markets across various regions. 
For British Columbia-based roles, the base salary hiring range for this position is CAD 87,450 to CAD 184,550. 
For Ontario-based roles, the base salary hiring range for this position is CAD 87,450 to CAD 137,450 annually. 
The range represents base salary only, and does not include company bonus, incentive for sales roles, equity or benefits, as applicable. 
This posting is to fill a vacancy on our team, unless otherwise noted.
